declarations.docstring: A subset of the representation space is polynomially dense when every polynomial vanishing on it vanishes identically.
Entrywise evaluation of the generic base-change coordinate matrix at a group element recovers the matrix underlying its component at the chosen vertex.
The algebra homomorphism that evaluates the localized base-change coordinate ring at a base-change group element.
On polynomials embedded in the localization, evaluation at a base-change group element agrees with multivariate polynomial evaluation at its coordinate values.
Composing evaluation at a base-change group element with the coordinate-ring pullback of an orbit map equals evaluation at the transformed representation.
Entrywise evaluation of the localized generic matrix at a base-change group element yields its matrix at the chosen vertex.
Entrywise evaluation of the localized generic inverse matrix at a base-change group element yields the inverse of its matrix at the chosen vertex.
If the base-change action has finitely many orbits over an infinite field, some representation has an injective coordinate-ring pullback along its orbit map.
For a base-change action with finitely many orbits over an infinite field, one orbit is polynomially dense in the representation space.
The assignment of coordinate variables obtained from the matrix entries of a base-change group element.
Polynomial density of a representation's orbit makes the coordinate-ring pullback along its orbit map injective.
The distinguished denominator of the base-change coordinate ring evaluates to a unit at every base-change group element.
The coordinate-value function obtained by reading every arrow-matrix entry of a quiver representation.
Reading the coordinates of the representation assembled from a coordinate-value function returns the original function.
The quiver representation assembled from a function assigning a scalar to each arrow-matrix coordinate.
